in_progress.meaning: How to mark a started ticket when not the default (GitHub: an `in progress` label), e.g. a GitHub Projects status field and value.

cap_mb.meaning: The memory cap, in MB, of each test command an agent or a merge runs on this machine (scripts/capped kills it over it); unset: this machine's share per slot, (memory - 2048 MB) / max_parallel - 1024 MB for the agent's own Claude, at least 512. A remote run uses its sandbox's own share instead.

cap_secs.meaning: The time cap, in seconds, of each test command an agent or a merge runs on this machine: a guard against a hung test, not a share.

merge_command.meaning: The repo's merge rule for task and ticket PRs, run by merge_task.py and ship_ticket.py merge in place of `gh pr merge <n> --squash --delete-branch --match-head-commit <sha>`, from the repo root with `{pr}` and `{sha}` filled in, e.g. `scripts/merge-pr.sh {pr}`; unset: that gh command, except that a ticket PR into the default branch of a repo with a `.review-gate.yml` is refused (no-merge-rule).

identity_command.meaning: A command printing a GitHub token for the identity build-epic opens, updates and merges PRs and updates the tracker as, run from the repo root before every gh call so no wait outlives the token, e.g. `scripts/gh-app-token.sh`; unset: the current gh login.

base.meaning: The branch a run's tickets are cut from, catch up with and open their PRs against, when not the default branch (a run's `--into <branch>` beats it); recorded once at setup as decisions.md's `base:`, which every step script reads; unset: the default branch.

merge_identity.meaning: Who merges task and ticket PRs, unless the run's decisions.md records `merge_identity:`: app (the identity_command token, which must answer `gh api installation/repositories`) or human (GH_TOKEN unset, and `gh api user` must be decisions.md's `human:` login); any other identity is refused (wrong-identity) and nothing merges.

task_merge_method.meaning: How task PRs merge into their ticket branch: squash (one commit per task; ship_ticket.py merge then records the integration ancestry with a guarded `git merge -s ours origin/<base>` before merging a ticket PR into a non-default base) or merge (merge commits, which keep the ancestry, so no ancestry step runs; passes `--merge` to a `merge-pr.sh` merge rule, and any other merge_command is refused, merge-method). Ticket PRs into the base merge by the merge rule either way.
